target_problem: unbalanced unate labels and exact gate-label behavior of Kuntewar-Sarma simple X certificates
conditional_implication: V99 gives deterministic polynomial-time range avoidance for every positive-surplus component whose essential gates lie in the singleton ternary NPN orbit, including explicit V97-irreducible families outside the V98 switching-balanced class. It also exactly classifies signed-MAJ3 simple X maps: the balanced switching class has exactly two missing edge words, while every nonzero switching class is surjective. This closes the simple-X forbidden-coloring route for unbalanced signed-majority labels but does not solve the surrounding circuit class.
frontier_reason: The singleton-core theorem is a genuine new tractable laboratory class beyond V98 balance, while the majority result is an exact local obstruction. The 48-table middle unate orbit and all non-unate labels remain open, so no published lower-bound-transfer threshold is crossed.

closed_route: extending the Kuntewar-Sarma simple-X MAJ forbidden-coloring certificate to unbalanced majority-of-literals labels merely by changing the target edge coloring
surviving_route: solve the 48-table unate NPN orbit represented by x AND (y OR z), then move to genuinely non-unate NPN classes using symbolic transfer systems or larger Turan substructures
current_gap: The middle essential-unate NPN orbit has fixed-output fibers expressible by 2-CNF, but range membership in P does not by itself construct a globally missing output. Signed-majority circuits in nonzero switching classes also require a certificate larger than the simple X because that local map is surjective.
stop_rule: Do not promote V100 from a finite truth-table or finite-cycle census. Require a symbolic constructor/classification for the 48-table middle unate orbit or a genuinely non-unate infinite family.
external_validation_target: Kuntewar-Sarma APPROX/RANDOM 2025 Lemma 26/Corollary 27 and Theorem 8; classical Harary/Zaslavsky signed-graph switching for terminology; targeted author review of the signed-MAJ simple-X dichotomy and singleton-core extension
